title: Radio (Vivid VH-109)
summary: Power, PoE vs barrel, link lights, programming, DS Wi-Fi in the pit.

start.question: Look at the five lights on the radio. What do you see?
start.help: Left to right: PWR, SYS, 2.4G, 6G, RIO.

options.label: PWR on, SYS blinking once a second
PWR on, SYS blinking very fast
Lights look fine but robot has no comms
Radio reboots or drops during a match
Team wants DS on Wi-Fi in the pit
PoE on the RIO port only
Both DC and PoE at the same time

dc-only.title: No power on the DC input
steps: Tug the Weidmuller plug at the radio. Pull the wires, strip fresh copper, push them back in until they lock.
Check polarity. Red to +, black to -. Reversed polarity does not light the radio.
Check the PDH or PDP channel that feeds the radio. Reseat the fuse or breaker. A red channel LED means no output.
Measure at the plug. The radio accepts battery voltage up to 19 V. No voltage means the wiring, not the radio.
12 V present and still dark: swap the radio and have it programmed at the kiosk. Tell the FTA.

poe-only.title: No power over PoE
steps: PoE comes in on the RIO port only. Move the cable if it is in AUX1, AUX2, or DS.
Check the injector or PoE cable is powered from a PDH or PDP channel with a good fuse.
Swap the Ethernet cable between injector and radio. A cable with a broken pair carries data but not power.
If the team has the DC plug wired too, use it instead and take the PoE power off.
Still dark: swap the radio, program it at the kiosk, tell the FTA.

dual-power.title: PoE and DC input at the same time
steps: Two power inputs from different sources or voltages makes the radio reboot or drop. This is a known bad setup seen in CSA tickets.
Pick one. Remove the power from the PoE injector and keep the Ethernet cable for data, or remove the DC plug.
Vivid allows dual feed only from the same source at the same voltage. Most teams do not have that. Use one.
Power cycle the radio after the change and wait 60 seconds for SYS.
If it still will not power, follow the DC only or PoE only branch of this guide.

rpm.title: Radio Power Module
steps: Do not power the radio from the RPM and the 12 V DC input at the same time. It can damage the radio.
Check the RPM input has 12 V from its PDH or PDP channel and its own LED is on.
Check the RPM output cable goes to the radio RIO port.
Vivid recommends fewer devices between the battery and the radio. Wire the radio straight to a PDH or PDP channel if the RPM is suspect.
Still dark: swap the radio and program it at the kiosk.

booting.title: PWR on, SYS off: still booting
steps: Wait 60 seconds. SYS stays off during boot.
If SYS never comes on after 2 minutes, power cycle the radio once.
A radio that loops power on and never finishes boot may be on old firmware with the flash corruption bug. Fixed in 1.2.5. Take it to the kiosk to update.
Check the supply voltage is steady. A weak battery or a loose plug can hold the radio in boot.
Still no SYS: swap the radio and tell the FTA.

where.question: Where is the robot right now?
where.help: SYS blinking once a second means the radio cannot ping the field access point.

options.label: In the pit or practice area

field-not-linked.title: On the field, radio cannot reach the AP
steps: Wait 60 seconds after power on.
Ask if the radio was programmed at this event's kiosk. If it came from home or another event, take it to the kiosk now.
Make sure only one radio is powered on the robot.
Check the DS is fully connected. The radio joins only after the DS is linked.
Check the radio is mounted in the open, not inside a metal frame or a printed box. Move it if needed.
Still blinking: swap the radio. Escalate to the FTA to check the field AP for this station.

pit-not-linked.title: In the pit, SYS blinking is normal
steps: In the pit there is no field AP, so SYS blinks. That is expected.
Connect the DS with an Ethernet cable into the radio DS port for pit testing.
If the team uses their own practice AP, it must be set up as an access point with the same key. That is not allowed on the event floor.
Do not reprogram the radio at home settings. It must stay on this event's kiosk settings.

flashing.title: SYS blinking very fast: firmware update
steps: 20 Hz blink means firmware is being written. 50 Hz means the first boot after an update.
Do not power off. Wait until SYS goes solid or slow blink. This can take 2 minutes.
If it has been more than 5 minutes, power cycle once and take it to the kiosk to check the firmware version.
Still stuck: swap the radio.

ap-battery.title: All lights blinking: AP mode on battery
steps: The radio is configured as an Access Point and sees battery power. Wireless is off.
Take it to the kiosk and program it in Robot Radio mode for this event.
If the team has an AP radio for practice, check they did not put it on the robot by mistake.
Still blinking after a reprogram: swap the radio.

rio-link.title: RIO light off: no link to the roboRIO
steps: The roboRIO must plug into the port labeled RIO. Move the cable if it is in AUX1, AUX2, or DS.
Check the RIO is powered and past boot. Its Status light should be off.
Reseat both ends of the Ethernet cable. Replace a cable with a broken latch.
Swap the cable for a known good one.
If the RIO Ethernet port is dead, a USB Ethernet adapter in the RIO USB port works as a stand-in. Use the roboRIO guide in this app.

programmed.question: Was this radio programmed at this event's kiosk?

reprogram.title: Program the radio at the kiosk
steps: Take the radio, or the robot, to the radio kiosk. Enter the team number. The kiosk sets the event key and updates firmware if needed.
Do not use the radio's own web page at an event. Only the kiosk has the right key.
After programming, power the radio from the robot and wait 60 seconds. SYS goes solid on the field.
If the kiosk cannot see the radio, plug the laptop into the DS port on the radio and try again. Then swap the cable.
Kiosk keeps failing on this radio: swap the radio and tell the FTA.

radio-ok.title: Radio looks healthy. The problem is downstream.
steps: SYS solid and RIO lit means the radio has the field and the RIO. Look elsewhere.
Check the DS: Enet Link, team number, FMS light. Use the Driver station guide in this app.
Check the roboRIO Comm light. Off means the RIO is not talking to the DS. Use the roboRIO guide.
Ping 10.TE.AM.2 from the DS laptop to test the RIO through the radio.
If everything pings but the DS stays red, escalate to the FTA.

reboots.title: Radio reboots or drops in matches
steps: If PoE and the DC input are both connected, remove one. Dual power caused reboots in this season's tickets.
Tug the Weidmuller plug. Re-strip and reseat the wires. Tie-wrap the cable to the frame near the radio so vibration does not pull on it.
Check the wire gauge and route. Thin wire on a long run drops voltage under load. Wire the radio to its own PDH or PDP channel.
Open the DS log. A battery dip below 7 V during a match resets the radio too. Lower motor current limits and use a good battery.
Check nothing else is on the radio's channel. A shared channel with a motor browns out the radio.
Still dropping: swap the radio and ask the FTA to watch the AP side.

ds-wifi.title: DS on Wi-Fi in the pit
steps: At an event, the kiosk decides if the 2.4 GHz pit network is on. Many events turn it off. Use an Ethernet cable into the radio DS port instead.
If 2.4 GHz is allowed, the network name is the team number plus the suffix set at the kiosk. The password is the 2.4 GHz key the team chose.
DIP switch 3 on the radio forces standalone 2.4 GHz mode at home. Leave it off at events.
Before a match, turn the laptop Wi-Fi off. On the field only Ethernet works.
If the team cannot find the network, check with the FTA whether 2.4 GHz is enabled at this event.
